selected.title: The effects of jump training on measures of physical performance, lower extremities injury incidence and burden in highly trained male soccer players.

before.aiReason: Single-blind randomized controlled trial in semi-professional male association football players comparing a 16-week jump-training program with regular soccer training, with lower-extremity injury incidence and burden as outcomes. It applies the UEFA epidemiological injury definition (time-loss) and records individual training and match exposure in hours, reporting injuries per 1000 h and days absence per 1000 h, giving a usable direct-time denominator. RCT epidemiology with a usable denominator is eligible under the criteria.
before.aiEvidenceQuote: A single blind (i.e., researchers) randomized controlled trial was conducted to compare the effects of 16-week jump training program (EG) compared to 16 weeks of regular soccer training (CG) in physical performance and lower extremities injury profile of semi-professional male soccer players. | The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) guidelines for epidemiological research were followed. Injury was defined as 'an injury that occurred during a scheduled training session or match that caused absence from the next training session or match'. | The lower extremities injury incidence (injuries/1,000 h exposure ...) was 8.94 in the CG compared to 2.81 in the EG ... Lower extremities injury burden (days of absence/1;000 h exposure ...) was 194.86 in the CG compared to 71.37 in the EG.
before.aiSourceLocation: Page 4, Experimental design and procedures | Page 6, Injuries: definitions and data collection | Page 10, Results

aiRawResponse.title: The effects of jump training on measures of physical performance, lower extremities injury incidence and burden in highly trained male soccer players.
aiRawResponse.reason: Single-blind randomized controlled trial in semi-professional male association football players comparing a 16-week jump-training program with regular soccer training, with lower-extremity injury incidence and burden as outcomes. It applies the UEFA epidemiological injury definition (time-loss) and records individual training and match exposure in hours, reporting injuries per 1000 h and days absence per 1000 h, giving a usable direct-time denominator. RCT epidemiology with a usable denominator is eligible under the criteria.
aiRawResponse.auditNotes: Included as eligible RCT epidemiology with UEFA time-loss definition and direct exposure-hour denominator for injury incidence and burden, despite small single-club sample. Reviewing model substituted to Claude Opus 4.8 (project-default GPT-5.5 quota-blocked until 2026-06-29); criteria fifa-gbi-full-text-v8-2026-06-23. No protected human/resolver fields touched.
aiRawResponse.dataSource: Club strength/conditioning and medical staff records using a UEFA-based standardized injury report and daily individual exposure logs.
evidenceQuotes: A single blind (i.e., researchers) randomized controlled trial was conducted to compare the effects of 16-week jump training program (EG) compared to 16 weeks of regular soccer training (CG) in physical performance and lower extremities injury profile of semi-professional male soccer players.

The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) guidelines for epidemiological research were followed. Injury was defined as 'an injury that occurred during a scheduled training session or match that caused absence from the next training session or match'.

The lower extremities injury incidence (injuries/1,000 h exposure ...) was 8.94 in the CG compared to 2.81 in the EG ... Lower extremities injury burden (days of absence/1;000 h exposure ...) was 194.86 in the CG compared to 71.37 in the EG.
aiRawResponse.derivationBasis: Exposure hours recorded and incidence/burden expressed per 1000 h; no reviewer calculation required.
sourceLocations: Page 6, Injuries: definitions and data collection
aiRawResponse.outcomeEligibility: Lower-extremity injury incidence (injuries/1000 h) and burden (days absence/1000 h) with rate ratios; eligible injury epidemiology outcome.
aiRawResponse.reportedDenominator: Individual training and match exposure recorded daily in hours; incidence expressed per 1000 h (CG 8.94 vs EG 2.81 injuries/1000 h) and burden per 1000 h (CG 194.86 vs EG 71.37 days/1000 h).
aiRawResponse.dataCollectionTiming: Prospective during a 16-week in-season intervention period; injuries and exposure recorded daily.
aiRawResponse.populationEligibility: Semi-professional senior male soccer players from one club, in-season (4 training sessions plus one official match per week).
aiRawResponse.injuryIllnessDefinition: Injury defined per UEFA guidelines as an injury occurring during a scheduled training session or match causing absence from the next training session or match; burden as days lost per 1000 h exposure.
aiRawResponse.denominatorEvidenceQuote: Data related to lower extremity injuries (i.e., incidence and burden) are presented as the number of injuries/1,000 h ... and the number of absence days/1,000 h ... Exposure time was registered daily individually, in hours, in training, and matches (friendly and official).
aiRawResponse.denominatorSourceLocation: Page 6, Injuries: definitions and data collection; Page 7, Statistical analysis; Page 11-12, Results.
